A snare is a trap — specifically, one that works by catching and holding something, usually without the trapped thing realising what is happening until it is too late. Think of it as a hidden danger that grabs you the moment you step into it.
Meaning 1: A Physical Trap for Animals

The most literal meaning of snare is a simple trap made of a looped wire, cord, or rope, set on the ground to catch animals — typically birds, rabbits, or other small creatures. The loop lies flat and hidden. When an animal walks through it, the loop tightens around its leg, foot, or neck, and the animal cannot escape.

What makes a snare different from other traps is its simplicity and sneakiness. There is no cage, no bait mechanism, no heavy machinery. It is just a quiet, hidden loop waiting patiently. The animal has no idea it is in danger until it is already caught.

Example sentences:

  • The hunter set a snare along the rabbit's trail.
  • The bird's leg was caught in a snare hidden in the tall grass.
Meaning 2: A Figurative Trap (The Most Common Modern Use)

This is where the word gets really powerful. In everyday language, people use snare to describe anything that traps, deceives, or lures a person into a bad situation — even when there is no physical trap involved at all.

Just like an animal doesn't see the wire loop until it's too late, a person caught in a figurative snare often doesn't realise the danger until they are already stuck. The "trap" here could be a bad relationship, a clever lie, a financial scheme, an addiction, a temptation, or any situation that is easy to fall into but very hard to get out of.

The key feeling the word carries is this: you were drawn in, you didn't fully see it coming, and now you are trapped.

Example sentences:

  • He fell into the snare of gambling and lost everything.
  • The con artist's friendly words were a snare designed to steal her money.
  • Pride can be a snare — it stops you from asking for help when you need it.
  • The seemingly great job offer turned out to be a snare full of impossible conditions.

Notice how in all these cases, the snare is invisible or disguised at first. That is the word's defining quality — it implies deception or hidden danger, not just any ordinary problem.
Meaning 3: The Snare of a Snare Drum

You may have seen or heard a snare drum — the shallow, sharp-sounding drum used in bands, orchestras, and marching groups. The word snare here refers to the set of thin metal wires or cords stretched tightly across the bottom of the drum.

When the drum is hit on the top, these wires vibrate against the bottom skin, producing that distinctive crisp, rattling, cracking sound that makes a snare drum sound completely different from other drums. These wires are called "snares" because, historically, they were made from animal gut or wire that resembled the cords used in trapping snares.

Example sentence:

  • The drummer adjusted the snares on his drum to get a tighter, crisper sound.

In medicine, a snare is a thin wire loop attached to a handle, used by doctors to remove unwanted growths (like polyps) from inside the body. The doctor slides the loop around the growth and tightens it — exactly like a trapping snare — to cut it off safely. This tool is commonly used during procedures like a colonoscopy.

Example sentence:

  • The surgeon used a snare to remove the polyp during the procedure.
The One Thread Connecting All Meanings

No matter which meaning you are looking at, the word snare always carries the same central idea: a loop or mechanism that catches and holds by tightening or closing in, whether that is around an animal's leg, a person's choices, a drum's vibrating skin, or a growth inside the body.

The emotional weight of the word — especially in its figurative use — is danger that creeps up quietly. It is not a punch; it is a trap. Not loud, not obvious — but inescapable once you are in it.

Snare (noun):

  1. A looped wire/cord trap used to catch animals
  2. (Figurative) Anything that deceives or lures a person into a difficult, dangerous, or inescapable situation
  3. The thin metal wires on the underside of a snare drum
  4. A wire-loop medical instrument used to remove growths
